## Button (Actions)
The control for starting an action, like saving, submitting or opening something. It comes in a few weights, from a strong primary button to quieter ones for secondary actions.
- Classes: `.ayy-button` `.ayy-button--secondary` `.ayy-button--outline` `.ayy-button--ghost` `.ayy-button--destructive` `.ayy-button--link` `.ayy-button--ring` `.ayy-button--xs` `.ayy-button--xl` `.ayy-button--sm` `.ayy-button--lg` `.ayy-button--icon` `.ayy-button--icon-sm` `.ayy-button--icon-xs` `.ayy-button--icon-xl` `.ayy-button--icon-lg` `.ayy-button--block` `.ayy-button--start` `.ayy-button--end` `.ayy-button-split` `.ayy-button-split--block`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, loading
- Sizes: `xs` `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` `icon-xs` `icon` `icon-sm` `icon-lg` `icon-xl`
- JS: buttonClass({ variant?, size?, block?, align?, className? }) → string; splitButtonClass({ block?, className? }) → string. Loading in HTML: aria-busy="true" plus <span class="ayy-spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span> as the first child.
- A11y: Icon-only buttons need aria-label and should always have a visible Tooltip on hover/focus. In a SplitButton, give the trailing menu trigger an explicit aria-label naming what it opens ("More deploy options"). Use disabled on <button>; on <a> use aria-disabled="true" (the class handles both). Visible focus ring on :focus-visible is built in — never remove it. While it works, set aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: loading). Don't disable it: focus would jump away.

## Hover actions (Actions)
Small buttons that appear over a picture, a video or a card when someone points at it, for quick actions like copy, annotate or pin. They stay out of the way until needed, and a tooltip names each one.
- Classes: `.ayy-hover-actions` `.ayy-hover-actions--top-start` `.ayy-hover-actions--top-end` `.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-start` `.ayy-hover-actions--bottom-end` `.ayy-hover-actions--group` `.ayy-hover-actions--reveal` `.ayy-hover-action`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, revealed
- JS: hoverActionsClass({ position?, group?, reveal?, className? }) → string; hoverActionClass({ className? }) → string
- A11y: Every button needs an aria-label (React's label sets it); the icon is decorative. Revealed rows are still in the tab order: focusing a button shows the row, so keyboard users reach every action. Touch screens have no hover, so --reveal rows always show there; never hide the only way to do something behind hover.

## Toolbar (Actions)
A row or column of tools for one surface, like an editor, a canvas or a text selection. It's a single tab stop with arrow keys between the tools, and can be fixed, floating or vertical.
- Classes: `.ayy-toolbar` `.ayy-toolbar--vertical` `.ayy-toolbar--floating` `.ayy-toolbar--scroll` `.ayy-toolbar--sm` `.ayy-toolbar__group` `.ayy-toolbar__separator` `.ayy-toolbar__spacer` `.ayy-toolbar__button`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md`
- Element: `<ayy-toolbar>`, events `ayy-press`
- JS: toolbarClass({ vertical?, floating?, scroll?, size?, className? }) → string; toolbarButtonClass, toolbarGroupClass, toolbarSeparatorClass, toolbarSpacerClass constants; connectToolbar(el) → { refresh, destroy } wires the keyboard pattern on plain markup.
- A11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label. Tab reaches it once (the last tool used, else the pressed one, else the first); Left/Right (Up/Down when vertical) move between tools, mirrored in RTL; Home/End jump to the ends. Disabled tools are skipped. Every icon-only tool needs an aria-label ("Rectangle"), and the name shouldn't change with its state — aria-pressed says whether it's on. Text fields and radio groups (swatches, a segmented control) inside keep their own arrow keys; the radio group is one stop. On is a wash tile with a hairline, not colour alone; High Contrast fills it with the system highlight.

## Action bar (Actions)
A bar that appears at the bottom of the screen once someone selects rows or cards in a table, grid or list. It shows how many are selected and offers actions that apply to all of them, such as archive or delete. It goes away when the selection is cleared.
- Classes: `.ayy-action-bar` `.ayy-action-bar--fixed` `.ayy-action-bar__selection` `.ayy-action-bar__count` `.ayy-action-bar__close` `.ayy-action-bar__separator` `.ayy-action-bar__actions` `.ayy-action-bar__button` `.ayy-action-bar__button--primary` `.ayy-action-bar__button--secondary` `.ayy-action-bar__button--destructive` `.ayy-action-bar__button--icon`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, open
- Element: `<ayy-action-bar>`, events `ayy-clear`
- JS: actionBarClass({ fixed?, className? }) → string; actionBarButtonClass({ variant?, primary?, secondary?, destructive?, icon?, className? }) → string; actionBarSelectionClass, actionBarCountClass, actionBarCloseClass, actionBarSeparatorClass, actionBarActionsClass constants; connectActionBar(bar, { onClear? }) → { refresh, syncCount, destroy } wires keyboard navigation, Escape/close clearing, and count updates.
- A11y: role="toolbar" with an aria-label ("Bulk actions"): one Tab stop, Left/Right arrow keys (mirrored in RTL) and Home/End move between the clear button and actions. Pressing Escape or clicking ActionBarClose clears the selection and dismisses the bar. Icon-only buttons inside the bar must have an aria-label (e.g. aria-label="Delete selected") and always be wrapped in a Tooltip. High Contrast mode borders the bar in CanvasText and highlights primary or open buttons with Highlight.

- A11y: Opening moves focus to the first item; arrows move, Home/End jump, letters jump to matching items. ArrowRight / ArrowLeft open and close submenus (mirrored in RTL); Esc inside a submenu closes only that panel. Esc or Tab closes the menu and focus returns to the trigger. A submenu panel holding more than items (an Icon picker) is role="dialog" and sits outside the menu, which may only hold items: in HTML right after it, named by its row's aria-controls; in React, the DropdownMenuSub wraps the DropdownMenuContent and the DropdownMenuSubContent follows it. Label the button with its row ("More options for Duplicate project"), not just "More".

## Command palette (Actions)
A search box above a list of actions and places, so people can find and run things from the keyboard. It can sit inline on a page or in a popover, or open as a dialog from a shortcut.
- Classes: `.ayy-command` `.ayy-command__search` `.ayy-command__input` `.ayy-command__list` `.ayy-command__group` `.ayy-command__label` `.ayy-command__item` `.ayy-command__content` `.ayy-command__title` `.ayy-command__description` `.ayy-command__meta` `.ayy-command__empty` `.ayy-command__footer`
- States: focus, disabled, selected, empty, filtered
- Element: `<ayy-command shortcut manual>`, events `ayy-select`
- JS: connectCommand(root, { onSelect?, filter?, reorder? }) → { refresh(activateFirst?), reset, destroy } wires filtering, the arrows, Enter and the pointer on plain markup; Enter clicks the highlighted item. Better matches move up (reorder: false when a framework owns the items; React Command ranks its children itself). commandMatches(text, query) is the matching rule (every typed word starts a word, or one word anywhere); commandItemText(item); commandItemDetails(item); commandScore(title, description, keywords, query). commandClass, commandInputClass, commandListClass, commandItemClass, commandSearchIcon (SVG markup).
- A11y: The WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox that is always shown: focus stays in the input, aria-activedescendant names the highlighted item, and the first match is highlighted as you type. Up/Down move (wrapping), PageUp/PageDown move five, Enter runs the highlighted item, Esc clears the field and a second Esc closes the dialog. Groups are role="group" named by their heading, so screen readers say "Go to" when the highlight enters one. Shortcuts in items are read as words ("Command N"); icons are hidden. The dialog palette is a modal <dialog> named by aria-label; focus goes to the input when it opens and back to the trigger when it closes.

## Floating action button (Actions)
A round floating button for the main action of a phone screen, like composing or adding something. It stays in the corner over the content and can show a label when extended.
- Classes: `.ayy-fab` `.ayy-fab--extended` `.ayy-fab--secondary` `.ayy-fab--lg` `.ayy-fab--sm` `.ayy-fab--inline`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: fabClass({ variant?, size?, extended?, inline?, className? }) → string; fabVariants, fabSizes.
- A11y: An icon-only FAB needs an aria-label that says the action ("New task"), not the icon ("Plus"). Put it after the main content in the DOM so it comes after what it acts on in the tab order, not before the page. It must not cover content for good: the App shell keeps it out of the bottom nav, and lists need room at their end (padding-block-end of the FAB's height) so the last row can scroll clear of it.

## Navbar (Navigation)
The header at the top of a website, with the brand on one side and links and actions on the other. It stays in view as the page scrolls, and on phones the links fold into a menu.
- Classes: `.ayy-navbar` `.ayy-navbar__inner` `.ayy-navbar__brand` `.ayy-navbar__nav` `.ayy-navbar__link` `.ayy-navbar__actions` `.ayy-navbar__toggle`
- States: hover, focus, selected, open
- Element: `<ayy-navbar>`
- JS: navbarClass, navbarInnerClass, navbarBrandClass, navbarNavClass, navbarLinkClass, navbarActionsClass, navbarToggleClass constants; connectNavbar(header) wires the phone menu and returns a cleanup; navbarMenuIcon (the Hugeicons menu icon as SVG markup).
- A11y: Use <header> for the bar and <nav aria-label="Main"> for the links; one main nav per page. Mark the current page with aria-current="page", not only with colour. Put a .ayy-skip-link before the navbar so keyboard users can jump past it. The menu button is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the nav (set for you). Focus stays on it when the panel opens; Tab moves into the links, Esc closes the panel and returns focus to the button. The closed panel is display: none, so its links are out of the tab order until it opens.

## App shell (Navigation)
The frame around a web app: a sidebar for navigation next to a main area where the content lives. On phones the sidebar turns into a bottom tab bar or a drawer. The same frame also holds settings screens.
- Classes: `.ayy-app-shell` `.ayy-app-shell__sidebar` `.ayy-app-shell__brand` `.ayy-app-shell__logotype` `.ayy-app-shell__nav` `.ayy-app-shell__link` `.ayy-app-shell__row` `.ayy-app-shell__more` `.ayy-app-shell__group` `.ayy-app-shell__group-label` `.ayy-app-shell__group--collapsible` `.ayy-app-shell__link--action` `.ayy-app-shell__list` `.ayy-app-shell__sublist` `.ayy-app-shell__collapse` `.ayy-app-shell__link--sub` `.ayy-app-shell__footer` `.ayy-app-shell__main` `.ayy-app-shell__bar` `.ayy-app-shell--settings` `.ayy-app-shell__back` `.ayy-app-shell__head` `.ayy-app-shell__title` `.ayy-app-shell__toggle` `.ayy-app-shell--collapsed` `.ayy-app-shell--hover-preview` `.ayy-app-shell--drawer` `.ayy-app-shell__detail` `.ayy-app-shell__resize` `.ayy-app-shell__resize--detail` `.ayy-app-shell--resizing` `.ayy-app-shell--md` `.ayy-app-shell--sm`
- States: hover, focus, selected, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-app-shell size collapsed hover-preview>`, events `ayy-collapse-change`, `ayy-resize`
- JS: appShellClass, appShellSidebarClass, appShellBrandClass, appShellNavClass, appShellLinkClass, appShellRowClass, appShellMoreClass, appShellFooterClass, appShellMainClass, appShellGroupClass, appShellGroupLabelClass, appShellGroupCollapsibleClass, appShellListClass, appShellSublistClass, appShellCollapseClass, appShellLinkSubClass, appShellBarClass, appShellToggleClass, appShellCollapsedClass, appShellHoverPreviewClass, appShellSmClass, appShellMdClass, appShellDrawerClass, appShellDetailClass, appShellResizeClass, appShellResizeDetailClass, appShellResizingClass, appShellSizes constants; appShellSettingsClass, appShellBackClass, appShellTitleClass, appShellHeadClass, appShellLogotypeClass constants; connectAppShell(shell, options) wires the phone drawer, desktop sidebar collapse and hover preview, and Esc in settings, and returns a cleanup; syncAppShellToggle(toggle, collapsed) sets a sidebar toggle's aria-expanded and its state label and tooltip text; appShellMenuIcon (the Hugeicons menu icon as SVG markup); appShellBackIcon (the settings back arrow, mirrored in RTL).
- A11y: The sidebar is an <aside> (a complementary landmark) and the content is a <main>: one <main> per page, and no other element with that landmark. Keep one <nav aria-label="Main"> in the sidebar. The bottom nav repeats its top destinations and only one of the two shows at a time, so it can use the same label. Give any other nav (a settings menu) its own label. Mark the current page with aria-current="page" in both the sidebar and the bottom nav. The link also gets a tint and a heavier weight, so colour is not the only cue; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight. Put a .ayy-skip-link before the shell, pointing at an id on <main>, so keyboard users can jump past the sidebar. A row's __more is a real button after the link, not inside it (buttons can't nest), and its aria-label names the row ("Project options") so a list of identical "More" buttons isn't ambiguous. Group with a heading and a list: the <p> label names the <ul> through aria-labelledby, so a screen reader announces "Workspace, list, 3 items". A collapse is a native <details>: Enter and Space toggle it, and the open state is exposed for you. Don't add aria-expanded to the <summary>. Mark the current child with aria-current="page" and open its collapse. A closed collapse that holds the current page is drawn bolder, so the location isn't hidden. Both columns are scroll containers. If a column can scroll but holds nothing focusable, give it tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it. The drawer's toggle is a real <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the sidebar (set for you). Opening moves focus to the first link in the drawer and makes the rest of the shell inert; Esc closes it and returns focus to the toggle. Settings mode: name the dialog by the sidebar title (aria-labelledby on the <dialog>), give the sections' nav its own label ("Settings"), mark the open section with aria-current="page", and make the section's Top bar title its <h1> (the sidebar title is an <h2>). Render the main as a <div> so the page keeps one <main>. On phones, opening a section moves focus to the main, and its back button returns it to the section's link. A collapsed sidebar with hover preview opens when keyboard focus moves into it (:focus-visible), so every link is reachable and readable from the keyboard; links without an icon are only in the tab order while it's open. Give rail links a title for a tooltip with the pointer. The sidebar's collapse toggle says what it does: in React, its aria-label and tooltip change between "Collapse sidebar" and "Expand sidebar" with the state, so the icon is never a guess. In plain markup, write the label and an <ayy-tooltip> for the state shown. In a dialog, Esc closes settings and focus returns to what opened them. A settings shell on a page of its own leaves through its __back on Esc, except when focus is in a text field or an open menu, popover or dialog has it. A resize handle is a separator you can focus: arrow keys move the edge by 16px (Shift 64), Home and End jump to the limits, and aria-valuenow / min / max are kept in px. The detail pane is an <aside>: label it (aria-label) for what it shows, and move focus into it when you open it from the main area. The phone sidebar (closed drawer) is visibility: hidden, and the bottom nav is display: none from 48rem, so hidden links are out of the tab order and the accessibility tree.

## Bottom nav (Navigation)
The tab bar of a phone app. It keeps the main destinations at the bottom of the screen where a thumb can reach them, each with an icon and a short label. Inside an App shell it replaces the sidebar on phones.
- Classes: `.ayy-bottom-nav` `.ayy-bottom-nav--sm` `.ayy-bottom-nav--md` `.ayy-bottom-nav--lg` `.ayy-bottom-nav--compact` `.ayy-bottom-nav--icon-only` `.ayy-bottom-nav__link` `.ayy-bottom-nav__label`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: bottomNavClass({ size?, compact?, iconOnly?, className? }) → string; bottomNavSizes constant; bottomNavLinkClass, bottomNavLabelClass constants.
- A11y: It's a <nav>: give it an aria-label ("Main" by default in React). Inside an App shell only one of it and the sidebar shows at a time, so they can share the label. Mark the current page with aria-current="page". It also gets a pill and a heavier weight, so colour isn't the only cue; High Contrast mode fills the pill with the system highlight. Visible labels are recommended. When iconOnly is used, screen reader text is preserved via visually hidden labels. A "More" tab is a <button> with aria-expanded (set for you when it's an app shell toggle), not a link to "#". Each tab is at least the control height of its size tier (sm 28px, md 32px, lg 40px), maintaining comfortable touch targets. Outside an App shell, content above it needs bottom padding (or to end before it) so the last line isn't hidden behind the bar.

## Top bar (Navigation)
The header of a phone screen, with a back button, the screen title and a few actions. It stays at the top, and can hold a search bar or a segmented control beneath it.
- Classes: `.ayy-top-bar` `.ayy-top-bar--center` `.ayy-top-bar--large` `.ayy-top-bar__back` `.ayy-top-bar__title` `.ayy-top-bar__heading` `.ayy-top-bar__subtitle` `.ayy-top-bar__actions` `.ayy-top-bar__row`
- States: hover, focus
- JS: topBarClass({ center?, large?, className? }) → string; topBarBackClass, topBarTitleClass, topBarHeadingClass, topBarSubtitleClass, topBarActionsClass, topBarRowClass constants; topBarBackIcon (the back chevron's SVG markup, mirrored in RTL).
- A11y: The title is the page's <h1>, so a screen reader user knows where they landed after navigating. A chevron-only back button is named "Back" (translate it); with a visible name ("Lists") the text names it. Icon buttons in __actions each need an aria-label. Keep to three; put the rest in a Menu behind a More button. The chevron is directional, so it points right in RTL, where "back" is.

## Breadcrumb (Navigation)
A trail of links that shows where the current page sits in the site, from the top level down. It lets people jump back to any page above it.
- Classes: `.ayy-breadcrumb` `.ayy-breadcrumb--sm` `.ayy-breadcrumb--lg` `.ayy-breadcrumb--pill` `.ayy-breadcrumb__list` `.ayy-breadcrumb__item` `.ayy-breadcrumb__link`

- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: breadcrumbClass({ size?, pill?, className? }) → string; breadcrumbListClass, breadcrumbItemClass, breadcrumbLinkClass constants.
- A11y: Wrap it in <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> and use an <ol>, so it's announced as an ordered path. The current page is plain text with aria-current="page", not a link to itself.

## Pagination (Navigation)
Controls for moving between the pages of a long table or list: previous, next and page numbers. On phones it shrinks to the essentials.
- Classes: `.ayy-pagination` `.ayy-pagination--sm` `.ayy-pagination--lg` `.ayy-pagination__link` `.ayy-pagination__size` `.ayy-pagination__size-label` `.ayy-pagination__link--step` `.ayy-pagination__ellipsis`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: paginationClass, paginationEllipsisClass, paginationSizeClass, paginationSizeLabelClass constants; paginationRootSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class for the <nav>; md adds nothing; paginationSizeClass is the page size picker); paginationLinkClass({ step?, className? }) → string; paginationRange(page, count, siblings = 1) → (number | "…")[] — which pages to show, always the same number of slots.
- A11y: It's a <nav aria-label="Pagination">: give a second one on the page a different label. The current page has aria-current="page"; it's outlined and bolder as well as tinted. Previous and next say so in words; their arrows are decorative and mirror in right-to-left text. An end you can't go past is aria-disabled (or disabled): screen readers hear it's unavailable. After a page change in place, move focus to the top of the updated table or list, or announce the new range.

## Steps (Navigation)
A progress indicator for a short flow like sign-up or checkout. It shows which step you're on, which are done and which are still to come.
- Classes: `.ayy-steps` `.ayy-steps--sm` `.ayy-steps--lg` `.ayy-steps--vertical` `.ayy-steps__item` `.ayy-steps__label`

- JS: stepsClass({ size?, vertical?, className? }) → string; stepsItemClass, stepsLabelClass constants.
- A11y: It's an ordered list with aria-current="step" on the current item, so screen readers hear "step 2 of 4, current". Give the <ol> an aria-label ("Checkout progress"). Done steps say so in text, not only with a tick: put an .ayy-sr-only "Done: " before their label (React does it). The markers are generated content with empty alt text, so numbers aren't read twice.

## Table of contents (Navigation)
A table of contents for long pages. It lists links to the sections beside the content and highlights the one being read.
- Classes: `.ayy-toc` `.ayy-toc--sticky` `.ayy-toc__title` `.ayy-toc__bar` `.ayy-toc__toggle` `.ayy-toc__toggle-icon` `.ayy-toc__toggle-current` `.ayy-toc__toggle-caret` `.ayy-toc__list` `.ayy-toc__link` `.ayy-toc__number`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- Element: `<ayy-toc offset>`, events `ayy-value-change`
- JS: tocClass({ sticky?, className? }) → string; tocTitleClass, tocListClass, tocLinkClass, tocNumberClass, tocBarClass, tocToggleClass, tocToggleIconClass, tocToggleCurrentClass, tocToggleCaretClass constants; tocMenuIcon, tocChevronIcon SVG strings; connectToc(root, { offset?, onChange? }) → cleanup — the scrollspy and mobile menu.
- A11y: It's a <nav> with a name (the title via aria-labelledby, or aria-label="On this page"), so it shows up in landmark lists. The current section is aria-current="location", announced by screen readers, not only drawn as a colour bar. Links are ordinary in-page anchors: they work without JS, and the navbar's scroll-padding keeps targets clear of the sticky header. Links grow to a 40px target at touch density. On phones the visible title is hidden but still names the nav, and the sticky toggle pill is labeled via aria-label.

## Tree (Navigation)
A hierarchical list of folders, files or records: groups that open and close with a chevron, one selected row and arrow-key navigation. Use it to browse a folder or file structure, or as a picker inside a card.
- Classes: `.ayy-tree` `.ayy-tree--sm` `.ayy-tree--lg` `.ayy-tree__item` `.ayy-tree__row` `.ayy-tree__toggle` `.ayy-tree__icon` `.ayy-tree__label` `.ayy-tree__group` `.ayy-tree--compact`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, expanded
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-tree>`, events `ayy-select`, `ayy-activate`, `ayy-toggle`
- JS: treeClass({ size?, compact?, className? }) → root classes; treeItemClass, treeRowClass, treeToggleClass, treeIconClass, treeLabelClass, treeGroupClass constants; treeChevronIcon (the ArrowRight01Icon SVG, directional); connectTree(root, { onSelect?, onActivate?, onToggle? }) → { focus(id?), destroy() } — expansion, single selection, roving tabindex and keyboard movement on plain markup.
- A11y: The tree is a <ul role="tree"> with a name (label in React, aria-label in HTML); each node is a <li role="treeitem"> with aria-level, and children sit in a <ul role="group">. aria-expanded is only on parents and aria-selected is on every node, so the state is announced rather than drawn only as a wash. The toggle is decorative (aria-hidden) and the item's aria-label is the node label, never the toggle. One visible item has tabindex="0" and the rest -1 (a roving tab stop). Tab enters the tree on the selected node, then the arrow keys, Home and End move through the visible nodes: Right closes an open group or opens a closed one and steps into its first child, Left closes an open group or moves to the parent. Enter activates a node and Space selects it. Double-click activates too. A composing IME and fields inside a row (a rename input) keep their keys. aria-disabled="true" keeps a node readable and reachable by the keyboard while it refuses selection and activation; colour is backed by opacity and, in High Contrast, GrayText. Long labels wrap inside the row instead of scrolling the tree sideways, and touch density raises the rows to the 44px target.

## Field (Forms)
A wrapper that ties a label, an input and its hint or error message together with consistent spacing. Use it around any form control.
- Classes: `.ayy-field` `.ayy-field--inline` `.ayy-label` `.ayy-field__hint` `.ayy-field__error`

- JS: fieldClass({ inline?, className? }); labelClass, fieldHintClass, fieldErrorClass constants
- A11y: Label htmlFor/for must match the control id. Link hint/error to the control with aria-describedby; set aria-invalid="true" on the control when there's an error. The label dims automatically when the control inside the field is disabled.

## Input (Forms)
A single-line text field for names, emails, passwords, search and other short text. It can hold icons, addons and buttons inside the field.
- Classes: `.ayy-input` `.ayy-input--sm` `.ayy-input--lg` `.ayy-input-group` `.ayy-input-group--sm` `.ayy-input-group--lg` `.ayy-input-group__addon`

- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: inputClass({ size?, className? }) → string; inputGroupClass({ size?, className? }) → string; inputGroupAddonClass constant.
- A11y: Every input needs a label: wrap in a Field with a Label (for/id), or aria-label for search boxes. The input inside an InputGroup still needs its own label; icons and addons do not name it. Errors: aria-invalid="true" + aria-describedby pointing at the error text. Action buttons inside an InputGroup (show password, clear) must have an accessible aria-label and aria-pressed where applicable.

## PIN input (Forms)
One box per character for verification codes, two-factor authentication tokens and passcodes. Typing advances to the next box, Backspace steps back, and pasting or SMS autofill fills the whole code at once.
- Classes: `.ayy-pin-input` `.ayy-pin-input--sm` `.ayy-pin-input--lg` `.ayy-pin-input__group` `.ayy-pin-input__separator` `.ayy-pin-input__slot`

- JS: pinInputClass({ size?, className? }) → string; pinInputGroupClass, pinInputSeparatorClass, pinInputSlotClass constants; connectPinInput(root, { type?, onChange?, onComplete? }) → { value, setValue, clear, focus, destroy }.
- A11y: Wrap in a Field with a Label (or aria-labelledby on the group), and keep each slot's aria-label ("Digit 1 of 6"). The first slot carries autocomplete="one-time-code" so SMS and password-manager autofill populate the whole code. Digits always read left to right even in RTL layouts; ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move visually between slots.

## Search bar (Forms)
A rounded search field with a magnifier and a clear button, often used at the top of a phone list. It's a real search form, so phones show a search key on the keyboard.
- Classes: `.ayy-search-bar` `.ayy-search-bar--sm` `.ayy-search-bar--lg` `.ayy-search-bar__field` `.ayy-search-bar__input` `.ayy-search-bar__clear` `.ayy-search-bar__shortcut` `.ayy-search-bar__cancel`

- A11y: role="search" makes the form a search landmark. Name the input (aria-label, or a <label>) by what it searches ("Search tasks"). The clear button is a real button named "Clear search"; clearing puts focus back in the field. Esc in a type="search" input clears it in most browsers; Cancel is for leaving the search, not clearing it. Results that update as you type should say how many there are in a polite live region.

## Filter bar (Forms)
A bar that brings together everything needed to filter a list, table or feed: quick filter tabs, filter menus, search, and the filters currently applied with a way to clear them all.
- Classes: `.ayy-filter-bar` `.ayy-filter-bar--flush` `.ayy-filter-bar--sticky` `.ayy-filter-bar--sm` `.ayy-filter-bar__main` `.ayy-filter-bar__group` `.ayy-filter-bar__tabs` `.ayy-filter-bar__tab` `.ayy-filter-bar__tab-count` `.ayy-filter-bar__trigger` `.ayy-filter-bar__trigger-badge` `.ayy-filter-bar__active` `.ayy-filter-bar__summary` `.ayy-filter-bar__clear`

## Sorting (Forms)
A dropdown for choosing how a list, table or feed is ordered. It matches the filter bar and sits next to it.

Sort options inside the paired DropdownMenu use role="menuitemradio" and aria-checked for accessible single-choice state.

## Textarea (Forms)
A multi-line text field for longer text like comments and descriptions. It can grow as you type.
- Classes: `.ayy-textarea` `.ayy-textarea--sm` `.ayy-textarea--lg` `.ayy-textarea--autosize` `.ayy-textarea--mono`

## Mentions (Forms)
A multi-line text field that opens a floating suggestions list right at the caret when someone types @ or #, for tagging teammates, channels or issues inside comments and notes.
- Classes: `.ayy-mentions` `.ayy-mentions__textarea` `.ayy-mentions__anchor` `.ayy-mentions__listbox` `.ayy-mentions__option` `.ayy-mentions__body` `.ayy-mentions__label` `.ayy-mentions__handle`

- JS: blockEditorClass({ inset?, className? }) → string; connectBlockEditor(root, { value?, placeholder?, label?, readOnly?, mentions?, upload?, renderMath?, onChange?, onMentionClick? }) → { getValue, setValue, setOptions, focus, destroy }; blockEditorBlock(type, fields?) makes a block; blockEditorNormalize(value) cleans one; blockEditorToMarkdown, blockEditorFromMarkdown, blockEditorToHtml and blockEditorToText convert (no DOM needed); a callout's tone is info, success, warning or destructive (absent is default; Markdown uses GitHub alerts, [!NOTE] [!TIP] [!WARNING] [!CAUTION], and [!IMPORTANT] imports as info); blockEditorMentionHtml({ trigger, id, label }) is a mention chip for a block's html; blockEditorCodeLanguages lists the languages a code block offers (block.language holds the id, highlighted with Code block's tokenizer); blockEditorEmbed(url) says what an embed block shows; blockEditorCleanHtml(html) keeps only the inline HTML the editor makes. A record block stores { trigger, id, label } and exports as trigger plus label in text and Markdown, and as <p data-record="triggerid">label</p> in HTML; Markdown import does not turn that text back into a record block. An equation block stores escaped TeX; Markdown is a $$ fence, HTML is <div data-math>\[tex\]</div>, and renderMath(tex) supplies the shown HTML.
- A11y: Name the editor (aria-label in React, label on <ayy-block-editor>): it's a role="group" of lines, each a role="textbox" named by its type (Text, Heading 1, To-do list). Everything works from the keyboard: Enter, Backspace and the arrows move through blocks; Tab and Shift+Tab nest; Mod+Enter opens or closes a toggle, whose arrow is not a tab stop; in a table Tab and Shift+Tab move between cells (Tab in the last one adds a row), Enter goes down a row and adds one after the last, Mod+Enter adds a row below, the arrows leave the table at its first and last row, Mod+Shift+arrows move the row or column (dragging its grip does the same), a cell's Mod+/ or right-click opens its menu (Row ›, Column ›, Header row, Header column, Clear every cell, then the block actions), the row and column grips open a menu scoped to that row or column and select it (insert, duplicate, move, clear, delete — columns also sort, align and set width), and the block handle's menu holds the table-wide items (→ opens a group, ← or Esc goes back); a callout's block actions include Colour › (Default, Info, Success, Warning, Destructive); Esc selects the block (then ↑/↓, Shift+↑/↓, Delete, Mod+D, Mod+Shift+↑/↓, Enter to edit again); Mod+/ opens block actions, Mod+Alt+0–8 turns a block into another type, Mod+B/I/U, Mod+Shift+S, Mod+Shift+H (highlight), Mod+E and Mod+K format. Tab nests, so the way out of the editor is Esc twice, then Tab. Screen readers hear an equation's TeX, not its rendered math: the text line stays available (named Equation) and the rendered HTML is hidden. The / and mention menus keep focus in the line: ↑/↓ move through aria-activedescendant, Enter or Tab picks, Esc closes without closing a parent Dialog. The block actions menu takes focus and gives it back. Opening a row or column grip's menu selects that row or column (Esc closes the menu and leaves it selected). Delete or Backspace clears it, Mod+Backspace or Mod+Delete deletes it, Mod+D duplicates it, Mod+Shift+arrows move it (left and right follow the reading direction), Mod+C copies it (a row is tab-separated, a column is one value per line), Mod+X copies then clears it, and Esc puts the caret in its first cell. Clicking a cell clears the selection. Block selections, moves and failed uploads are read out in a polite live region. Images take their caption as alt text: write one for every picture that carries meaning.

## Inline edit (Forms)
A value that becomes an input where it sits: a page or card title, a project name, a version, a due date. Click it or press Enter to edit, Enter saves, Esc cancels, blur saves, and a multiline field grows as you type and saves on Mod+Enter.
- Classes: `.ayy-inline-edit` `.ayy-inline-edit__display` `.ayy-inline-edit__text` `.ayy-inline-edit__input` `.ayy-inline-edit--title`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, error, editing
- Element: `<ayy-inline-edit>`, events `ayy-change`, `ayy-edit`
- JS: inlineEditClass({ variant?, className? }) → root classes; inlineEditVariants; isComposingEvent(event) → true during IME composition; commitsOnEnter(event, multiline?) → whether that Enter saves; growInlineEdit(textarea) → size a textarea to its content; connectInlineEdit(root, { onCommit?, onCancel?, onEditingChange?, trim? }) → { start, commit, cancel, isEditing, destroy } wires plain markup.
- A11y: The display is a real button and the field is a real input: give both the same aria-label (label in React), written as the action ("Rename the project"), and keep it when the value changes. Enter saves, Esc cancels and puts focus back on the display button; blur and Tab save without pulling focus back. Enter while an IME is composing is left to the IME, so a Japanese, Chinese or Korean word can be confirmed without saving. The empty value shows the placeholder as text, not as the only name: the button keeps its aria-label.

## Select (Forms)
A dropdown for choosing one option from a list. It's the native select with a nicer list on desktop, and the system picker on touch devices.
- Classes: `.ayy-select` `.ayy-select__control` `.ayy-select__list` `.ayy-select__option` `.ayy-select__label` `.ayy-select__picture` `.ayy-select--sm` `.ayy-select--lg`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, error, open, multiple
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: selectClass({ size?, className? }) → string for the wrapper; selectControlClass, selectListClass, selectOptionClass, selectLabelClass constants; openSelectListFrom(event) opens the list from a mousedown or keydown on a select (what React Select and "@danitesler/ayywi/elements" call); openSelectList(select) opens it directly; usesSelectList(select) says whether a select gets the list here; selectPictureClass, selectPicture(select, value) and syncSelectPicture(select) (shows the chosen option's picture; @danitesler/ayywi/elements calls it on change). Choosing from ayywi's list fires input and change when the value changes, then a bubbling ayy-choose event (detail.value) on the select for every choice, the option already chosen included
- A11y: Label it like any input (Field + Label with for/id); the list takes the same name. The list is a role="listbox" of role="option"s: arrows, Home/End and type-ahead move, Enter, Space or a click chooses, Esc, Tab or a click outside closes, and focus goes back to the select. Touch screens keep the OS picker, which suits them better. Don't build your own dropdown for choosing a value: this is it. Pictures are aria-hidden: an option's text names it, in the list and in the OS picker.

## Combobox (Forms)
A text field that filters a list as you type, for picking one option from a long set like a city, a customer or a time zone. The options open under the field and follow the standard accessible pattern.
- Classes: `.ayy-combobox` `.ayy-combobox__listbox` `.ayy-combobox__option` `.ayy-combobox__meta` `.ayy-combobox__empty`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, error, open, empty
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-combobox manual>`, events `ayy-select`
- JS: connectCombobox(input, listbox, { onSelect?(option | null), filter? }) → { open, close, refresh, destroy } wires the pattern on plain markup; comboboxOptionLabel(option) and comboboxOptionByValue(listbox, value) read options; comboboxChevronIcon (SVG markup) and part class constants.
- A11y: Focus stays in the input: Down opens the list and moves through it, Up goes back, Enter picks, Esc closes (and a second Esc clears), Alt+Down opens without moving. Screen readers follow aria-activedescendant. Label the input with a <label for> its id; the chevron is decoration. Typing highlights the first match, so Enter picks it; options that don't match are hidden, and "No matches" shows when none do.

## Tag input (Forms)
A field that turns what you type into removable chips, for tags, labels or email recipients. It can also suggest options as you type.
- Classes: `.ayy-tag-input` `.ayy-tag-input__tag` `.ayy-tag-input__input` `.ayy-tag-input--sm` `.ayy-tag-input--lg`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, error, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-tag-input name max case-sensitive>`, events `ayy-change`
- JS: splitTags(text) → tags split at commas and new lines; addTags(values, add, { max?, caseSensitive? }) → values with the new ones appended (no duplicates, ignoring case); tagChip(value, removeLabel?) → a chip element; tagInputClass({ size?, suggestions?, className? }); tagRemoveIcon (SVG markup). connectTagInput(root, { name?, max?, caseSensitive?, onChange?, removeLabel?, addedText?, removedText? }) → { values, setValues, destroy } wires plain markup and draws the chips.
- A11y: Label the inner input with <Label htmlFor> on its id and describe how to add a tag in a FieldHint ("Press Enter or type a comma"). Each chip's × is a real button named "Remove design"; Backspace in the empty field removes the last tag too. Adding and removing are announced in a polite live region ("design added"), and focus stays in the input. With suggestions the input is a combobox: arrows move through them, Enter adds the highlighted one, and ones already added are aria-disabled.

## Record picker (Forms)
A tag field whose chips are records picked from a list: one person to assign, many labels to apply. Type to filter, Enter picks the active record, Backspace in the empty field removes the last, and a create row turns new text into a record.
- Classes: `.ayy-record-picker` `.ayy-record-picker--multiple` `.ayy-record-picker__tag` `.ayy-record-picker__tag-label` `.ayy-record-picker__input` `.ayy-record-picker__clear` `.ayy-record-picker__listbox` `.ayy-record-picker__option` `.ayy-record-picker__option-body` `.ayy-record-picker__option-label` `.ayy-record-picker__description` `.ayy-record-picker__create` `.ayy-record-picker__create-label` `.ayy-record-picker__empty`

It never changes chips or aria-selected.
- A11y: Label the input with <Label htmlFor> and aria-labelledby (or aria-label); the controller copies that name onto the listbox, so the list reads as "Assignee". The input keeps focus: arrows move aria-activedescendant, Enter picks, Escape closes and clears the query, and the pointer never moves focus into the list. In multiple mode the list is aria-multiselectable: picked records carry aria-selected and a check, and picking one again removes it. Each chip's × is named "Remove Ada Lovelace", and Backspace in the empty field removes the last chip.

## Transfer list (Forms)
A dual-list shuttle for moving items between an available column and a selected column, such as role permissions, export columns or team members. Each column supports live filtering, select-all and keyboard navigation.
- Classes: `.ayy-transfer-list` `.ayy-transfer-list__pane` `.ayy-transfer-list__header` `.ayy-transfer-list__title` `.ayy-transfer-list__count` `.ayy-transfer-list__search` `.ayy-transfer-list__filter` `.ayy-transfer-list__list` `.ayy-transfer-list__item` `.ayy-transfer-list__item-body` `.ayy-transfer-list__label` `.ayy-transfer-list__description` `.ayy-transfer-list__empty` `.ayy-transfer-list__actions`

## Color picker (Forms)
A panel for choosing any colour. It combines an area for shade and brightness, sliders for hue and transparency, a hex field and a row of preset colours.
- Classes: `.ayy-color-picker` `.ayy-color-picker__area` `.ayy-color-picker__handle` `.ayy-color-picker__sliders` `.ayy-color-picker__hue` `.ayy-color-picker__alpha` `.ayy-color-picker__preview` `.ayy-color-picker__inputs` `.ayy-color-picker__copy` `.ayy-color-picker__swatches` `.ayy-color-picker__swatch`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected
- Element: `<ayy-color-picker value alpha name>`, events `ayy-change`
- JS: colorPickerClass({ className? }) → string; connectColorPicker(root, { value?, alpha?, swatches?, onChange? }) → { setValue, update, destroy } wires the 2D area, sliders, hex input and preset swatches; hsvToRgb(hsv), rgbToHsv(rgb), rgbToHex(rgb), hexToRgb(hex) conversion functions.
- A11y: The 2D saturation/brightness area is a focusable role="slider" with aria-label, aria-valuetext, and arrow key navigation (Shift for 10% steps). Hue and alpha sliders are native range inputs with accessible labels, keyboard stepped navigation, and Home/End support. The hex input allows typing exact hex color codes with keyboard and screen reader support. In Windows High Contrast mode, the panel, sliders, swatches, and handle keep clear outlines using CanvasText and Highlight system colors.

## Icon picker (Forms)
A searchable grid of icons and emoji with a remove button, for marking a column, project, page or label with a symbol. It sits in a Popover or as the submenu panel of a Menu.
- Classes: `.ayy-icon-picker` `.ayy-icon-picker__header` `.ayy-icon-picker__search` `.ayy-icon-picker__remove` `.ayy-icon-picker__body` `.ayy-icon-picker__section` `.ayy-icon-picker__label` `.ayy-icon-picker__grid` `.ayy-icon-picker__option` `.ayy-icon-picker__empty`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, selected
- Element: `<ayy-icon-picker value name>`, events `ayy-change`
- JS: iconPickerClass({ className? }) → string; iconPickerOptionClass and the other part constants; iconPickerEmojis (a starter set of { value, label, keywords }); connectIconPicker(root, { onChange?, manageSelection? }) → { setValue, filter, refresh, destroy } wires search, the roving tab stop, arrow keys and picking. Every pick dispatches a bubbling "ayy-pick" event ({ value, kind, option }) from the root; a Menu around the picker closes on it.
- A11y: Every option is a <button> with an aria-label naming the icon or emoji (an emoji character alone is read inconsistently) and aria-pressed for the picked one, so the choice is announced, not only tinted. Each section is a role="group" labelled by its heading. One option is the tab stop (the picked one, or the first): Tab moves search → grid → remove, and the arrow keys, Home and End move inside the grid, mirrored in RTL. ArrowDown from the search field enters the grid and ArrowUp from the first row returns to it; Enter in the search field picks the first match. A no-match search announces the role="status" empty message. Keys stay inside the picker except Esc, so a Menu or Popover around it still closes on Esc and returns focus. As a menu's submenu panel, give the panel role="dialog" and an aria-label, put it after the menu rather than inside it (a menu holds only items), and give the trigger aria-haspopup="dialog".

## Checkbox (Forms)
A box for turning an option on or off, or for picking several items from a list. It's the native checkbox with a clearer look, and it can show a mixed state when only some of a group is selected.
- Classes: `.ayy-checkbox` `.ayy-checkbox--sm` `.ayy-checkbox--lg`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, error, indeterminate
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: checkboxClass constant; checkboxSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class; md adds nothing)
- A11y: A colour alone doesn't say what it means: keep the priority or status in the label too. Wrap it in a <label class="ayy-label"> with the text, or pair with <label for>. Indeterminate is announced as "mixed" automatically. Group related checkboxes in a <fieldset> with a <legend>.

## Radio (Forms)
A set of options where exactly one can be chosen. It's built on native radio buttons, grouped under a legend.
- Classes: `.ayy-radio` `.ayy-radio--sm` `.ayy-radio--lg` `.ayy-radio-group` `.ayy-radio-group--horizontal` `.ayy-radio-group--sm` `.ayy-radio-group--lg` `.ayy-radio-group__legend`

- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: radioClass, radioGroupLegendClass constants; radioSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class); radioGroupClass({ orientation?, size?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Arrow keys move between radios in a group natively — no JS needed. Always give the group a legend (label prop) and each radio a wrapping <label class="ayy-label">.

## Segmented control (Forms)
A short row of options where one is always selected, for switching a view, a range or a setting that changes what you see. It looks like tabs but works like radio buttons.
- Classes: `.ayy-segmented-control` `.ayy-segmented-control--sm` `.ayy-segmented-control--lg` `.ayy-segmented-control--full` `.ayy-segmented-control__option`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: segmentedControlClass({ size?, full?, className? }) → string; segmentedControlOptionClass constant.
- A11y: It's a radio group: give the root an aria-label ("Date range"). Arrow keys move the choice, Tab leaves the group — the browser does it. The checked segment is filled and bolder, not only coloured; High Contrast mode fills it with the system highlight. An icon-only segment needs text for screen readers: an .ayy-sr-only span or aria-label on the input.

## Chip (Forms)
A compact pill for filters and choices. Chips can be switched on and off, work as single or multiple choice, or be removable when they stand for filters that are applied.
- Classes: `.ayy-chip` `.ayy-chip--sm` `.ayy-chip--lg` `.ayy-chip--removable` `.ayy-chip__count` `.ayy-chip__remove` `.ayy-chip-group` `.ayy-chip-group--scroll`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: chipClass({ size?, removable?, className? }), chipGroupClass({ scroll?, className? }) → string; chipCountClass, chipRemoveClass constants; chipRemoveIcon (SVG markup of the cross).
- A11y: Checkbox and radio chips are native inputs: Space toggles, radios in a group move with the arrow keys, and screen readers announce "checked". Button chips announce "pressed". Give the group an aria-label naming what it filters ("Status"), and radio chips role="radiogroup". The on state is a border, a wash and a tick, not colour alone; High Contrast fills it with the system highlight. Every remove button needs an aria-label with the filter it removes. After removing one, move focus to the next chip or the search field so it isn't lost.

## Color swatch (Forms)
Round colour options for picking one colour, as for a tag, a list or a drawing tool. It can include a "no colour" option and an "any colour" option that opens the colour picker.
- Classes: `.ayy-swatch` `.ayy-swatch--sm` `.ayy-swatch--lg` `.ayy-swatch--none` `.ayy-swatch--custom` `.ayy-swatch-popover` `.ayy-swatch-group` `.ayy-swatch-group--track`

- A11y: Radio swatches are native: Tab enters the group, arrow keys move the pick, and screen readers say the colour's name and "checked". Every swatch needs a name (label prop / aria-label) because a dot has no text. Name the group ("Tag colour") with aria-label or aria-labelledby. The picked swatch has a ring and a tick, not just a colour; light and dark dots keep a hairline edge in every theme. High Contrast outlines the picked one with the system highlight. The dot is smaller than a touch target, but its hit area reaches a control's height (bigger at touch density).

## Choice card (Forms)
A large option for picking one or more things that need more explanation than a radio label, like plans, delivery methods or add-ons. The whole card is clickable and works as a normal radio or checkbox.
- Classes: `.ayy-choice-group` `.ayy-choice-group--sm` `.ayy-choice-group--lg` `.ayy-choice-group--scroll` `.ayy-choice-card--sm` `.ayy-choice-card--lg` `.ayy-choice-group__legend` `.ayy-choice-card` `.ayy-choice-card--compact` `.ayy-choice-card__title` `.ayy-choice-card__description` `.ayy-choice-card__meta`

- A11y: Each card is a native radio or checkbox labelled by the whole card: Space picks it, arrow keys move between radios, and the title, description and price are its name. Group them in a <fieldset> with a <legend> (ChoiceGroup legend) so the question is announced with each option. Chosen is a thicker border (and a filled card when compact), not colour alone; High Contrast outlines it with the system highlight. A full slot stays in the group as disabled, struck through, so people see what isn't available.

## Slider (Forms)
A control for choosing a value, or a range between two values, by dragging a handle along a track. It's a native range input, so the keyboard, forms and screen readers work as usual.
- Classes: `.ayy-slider--sm` `.ayy-slider--lg` `.ayy-slider-range--sm` `.ayy-slider-range--lg` `.ayy-slider` `.ayy-slider-range`

- A11y: It's a native range input: arrow keys step, Page Up/Down jump, Home/End go to the ends, and screen readers read the value. Give it a <label> (or aria-label); add aria-valuetext when the number needs a unit ("12 people"). Show the value in text next to the label (an <output>), so it doesn't depend on the thumb's position. Each thumb of a range has its own name ("Minimum price", "Maximum price"); name the group with aria-labelledby. The focus ring is on the thumb. In High Contrast the fill and the thumb take system colours.

A number input with minus and plus buttons, for small quantities like seats, guests or items. Typing and arrow keys work as in any number field.

At min or max the button gets aria-disabled instead of disabled, so focus stays on it while you click. The input is a real number field: type a value, or use the arrow keys.

## File upload (Forms)
An area for dropping files or clicking to choose them. It's a real file input underneath, so it works without extra code, and it pairs with a list to show what was picked.

Dragging is an extra: everything works with the picker alone. List the picked files in text, each with a remove button that names the file ("Remove studio-front.jpg"), and progress with a Progress bar that has a label.

## Switch (Forms)
An on/off control for a setting that takes effect right away. It's a native checkbox with a switch look and the right accessible role.

## Shortcut (Forms)
Keyboard shortcuts written once and shown correctly for each device. It also includes a recorder that lets people set their own shortcut, and a list for help screens.
- Classes: `.ayy-shortcut` `.ayy-shortcut-recorder` `.ayy-shortcut-recorder__placeholder` `.ayy-shortcut-list` `.ayy-shortcut-list__row`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, error
- Element: `<ayy-shortcut-recorder value label bare>`, events `ayy-change`, `ayy-recording`
- JS: Shortcuts are strings like "Mod+Shift+K" (Mod = ⌘ on Apple devices, Ctrl elsewhere; also Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Meta). shortcutFromEvent(event, { bare? }) → the shortcut a keydown makes, or null for modifiers alone; matchShortcut(event, "Mod+K") → boolean, for your own handlers, by physical key, so it works on any layout (Russian Cmd+У is Mod+E); shortcutKeys(s, platform?) → ["⌘", "K"] (Super on Linux, Win on Windows); shortcutLabel(s, platform?) → "Command K"; shortcutHtml(s, platform?) → markup; syncShortcuts(root?, platform?) redraws static .ayy-shortcut[data-keys] for Apple and Linux devices (@danitesler/ayywi/elements does it on load); getPlatform(); isApplePlatform(); isWindowsPlatform(); isLinuxPlatform(); keyFromCode(code). connectShortcutRecorder(button, { value?, label?, bare?, onChange?, onRecordingChange? }) → { setValue, destroy }. shortcutClass, shortcutRecorderClass({ className? }).
- A11y: Keycaps are aria-hidden and a visually hidden label says the keys in words ("Command Shift K"), so screen readers don't read "place of interest sign". The recorder is a toggle button: aria-pressed="true" while listening, and its aria-label says the action, the keys and how to cancel ("Capture area: Press keys, or Escape to cancel"). While it listens it takes every key, Tab included (Tab cancels and moves on), so it can never trap focus. Pause the app's own shortcuts while recording (onRecordingChange / ayy-recording), or pressing one would run it. A clash is shown with aria-invalid on the recorder and a hint saying which action already uses it; the border is not the only cue.

## Settings (Forms)
A layout for preferences as rows, with a label and a short hint on one side and the control on the other, grouped under headings. A row can also link to a sub-page or run an action like signing out.
- Classes: `.ayy-settings` `.ayy-settings--plain` `.ayy-settings__title` `.ayy-settings__description` `.ayy-settings__list` `.ayy-settings__row` `.ayy-settings__row--stack` `.ayy-settings__text` `.ayy-settings__label` `.ayy-settings__hint` `.ayy-settings__control` `.ayy-settings__link` `.ayy-settings__value` `.ayy-settings__link--destructive` `.ayy-settings__picker` `.ayy-settings__option` `.ayy-settings__preview` `.ayy-settings__caption` `.ayy-settings__screen` `.ayy-settings__screen--rows` `.ayy-settings__screen--brand`

A custom colour Select: settingsColorInput(select) finds the hidden <input type="color" data-value> right after its wrapper, openSettingsColor(select) opens ayywi's colour picker under the select when that option is chosen (call it on change and on ayy-choose, after the list closes), syncSettingsColor(input) shows the colour in that option's picture; @danitesler/ayywi/elements does all three page-wide. Apply the picks with setTheme(), setDensity() and setBrand(); data-motion="reduce" and dir for motion and direction.
- A11y: Each group is a <section> labelled by its <h2>, so screen-reader users can jump between groups. Every control needs a name: give SettingsRow htmlFor and the control that id, so the label is a real <label for>. For a Switch, put the id on the switch's input. Point the control's aria-describedby at the hint (`${htmlFor}-hint`) so the explanation is read with it. A link row is one <a> or <button>: its whole text, value included, is its name. Use <a href> when it opens a page, <button> when it does something. Controls wrap under the label on narrow screens instead of shrinking below a usable size. A picker is a radiogroup of native radios: arrow keys move between options, and each option is named by its caption. The pictures are aria-hidden. A custom colour's <input type="color"> is hidden and out of the tab order: choosing Custom opens the colour picker as a labelled dialog under the select with focus in it, and Esc or Enter closes it and puts focus back on the select.

## Page header (Layout)
The top of a screen in an app: the page title, a line of description and the page's main actions, with an optional breadcrumb above. On phones the actions move below the title.
- Classes: `.ayy-page-header` `.ayy-page-header__title` `.ayy-page-header__description` `.ayy-page-header__actions`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: pageHeaderClass, pageHeaderTitleClass, pageHeaderDescriptionClass, pageHeaderActionsClass constants.
- A11y: The title is the page's only <h1>; sections below it start at <h2>. Keep the actions after the title in the source, so screen readers hear what the page is before what it can do. A breadcrumb above the title is its own <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">.

## Showcase (Layout)
A container for previewing a design at different screen sizes. It has a toolbar for switching devices and can show the code behind the preview.

- A11y: Give the Showcase an aria-labelledby pointing to its ShowcaseTitle. Device switchers must have accessible labels describing the active viewport.

## Card (Layout)
A surface that groups related content so it reads as one unit, like a project, a summary or a block of settings. It can react to hover when it's clickable, and it has a media version for captures, recordings and pictures.
- Classes: `.ayy-card` `.ayy-card--sm` `.ayy-card--lg` `.ayy-card--interactive` `.ayy-card--spotlight` `.ayy-card--transparent` `.ayy-card--featured` `.ayy-card__header` `.ayy-card__title` `.ayy-card__description` `.ayy-card__content` `.ayy-card__footer` `.ayy-card__media` `.ayy-card__link` `.ayy-card--view` `.ayy-card__view-media` `.ayy-card__view-backdrop` `.ayy-card__view-image` `.ayy-card__view-badge` `.ayy-card__view-play` `.ayy-card__view-body` `.ayy-card__view-text` `.ayy-card__view-title` `.ayy-card__view-meta` `.ayy-card__view-badges`

- A11y: If the whole card is a link, put ayy-card__link on the title's <a> — don't wrap the card in <a>. Screen readers then announce just the title, not the whole card. Media images are content: give them alt text, or alt="" when the title already says it all. Spotlight layers are pseudo-elements, invisible to assistive tech. View cards: when the picture opens something, CardViewMedia is a <button> or <a> with an aria-label that names the item and the action ("Annotate the pricing page capture from 2 minutes ago"); the body is decoration on top of it. View cards reveal their body and actions on focus as well as hover, and always show them on touch screens, so nothing is hover-only. The backdrop is aria-hidden.

## Tabs (Layout)
Tabs for switching between panels of related content on the same page. They can be used fully from the keyboard.
- Classes: `.ayy-tabs` `.ayy-tabs--sm` `.ayy-tabs--lg` `.ayy-tabs__list` `.ayy-tabs__tab` `.ayy-tabs__panel` `.ayy-tabs__count`

- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-tabs value>`, events `ayy-value-change`
- JS: tabsClass/tabsListClass/tabsTabClass/tabsPanelClass/tabsCountClass constants; tabsSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class for the root; md adds nothing); nextTabIndex(key, current, count, rtl) for custom keyboard handling.
- A11y: Arrow keys move between tabs (flipped in RTL), Home/End jump to first/last. Activation follows focus. Only the selected tab is in the tab order (roving tabindex). Give the tablist an aria-label when there's no visible heading.

## Accordion (Layout)
A stack of sections that expand and collapse, for FAQs and for settings with a lot of detail. Only the heading shows until someone opens a section, and opening one can close the others.
- Classes: `.ayy-accordion` `.ayy-accordion--sm` `.ayy-accordion--lg` `.ayy-accordion__item` `.ayy-accordion__trigger` `.ayy-accordion__content`
- States: hover, focus, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: accordionClass, accordionItemClass, accordionTriggerClass, accordionContentClass constants; accordionSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class for the root; md adds nothing).
- A11y: It's native <details>/<summary>: Enter and Space toggle it and the open state is announced. Don't add aria-expanded or a click handler. Keep the summary text short and complete (a question), since it's the only part people see. Find-in-page opens a closed item that contains the match.

## Carousel (Layout)
A row of slides that scrolls sideways, with buttons to move to the next or previous one. It suits galleries, testimonials and featured items. It uses native scrolling, so swiping and the keyboard work without extra code.
- Classes: `.ayy-carousel` `.ayy-carousel__track` `.ayy-carousel__slide` `.ayy-carousel__controls`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled
- Element: `<ayy-carousel>`
- JS: carouselClass, carouselTrackClass, carouselSlideClass, carouselControlsClass constants; connectCarousel(root) → cleanup — wires the buttons, aria-disabled at the ends and slide labels.
- A11y: The root is a named region with aria-roledescription="carousel"; each slide is a group named "n of total" unless you name it. The track is focusable, so arrow keys scroll it; the buttons stay focusable at the ends (aria-disabled, not disabled) so focus isn't lost. Nothing moves on its own, and smooth scrolling turns off under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Separator (Layout)
A thin line that divides blocks of content, between sections of a page or between items in a row.
- Classes: `.ayy-separator` `.ayy-separator--vertical` `.ayy-separator--fade`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: separatorClass({ orientation?, fade?, className? }) → string
- A11y: <hr> is a separator to screen readers. If the line is purely decorative, use role="presentation" or a CSS border instead. Vertical separators need aria-orientation="vertical" (the React component adds it).

## Scrollbar (Layout)
A thin scrollbar with no track that is drawn in the text colour, so it follows every theme. Put it on any scroll container, or on the page.
- Classes: `.ayy-scrollbar` `.ayy-scrollbar--hover`
- States: hover, pressed, focus
- JS: scrollbarClass({ hover?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Scrolling stays native: wheel, touch, keyboard and assistive technology all work. The component only changes how the bar looks. A scroll container that has no focusable content needs tabindex="0" and a label, or keyboard users can't scroll it. The React component sets tabindex="0". Forced colours: the thumb is drawn in system colours.

## Drag and drop (Layout)
Standard drag and drop for reordering items and moving them between areas: a floating preview follows the pointer, drop targets show hover states (ready, over, reject), and a primary line indicates the exact drop position. Fully accessible with arrow keys.
- Classes: `.ayy-draggable` `.ayy-drag-handle` `.ayy-sortable` `.ayy-sortable--horizontal` `.ayy-sortable__item` `.ayy-drop-target` `.ayy-drag-preview` `.ayy-drag-preview--chip`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, disabled, error, dragging, ready, over, edge
- Element: `<ayy-drag-drop orientation handle areas>`, events `ayy-move`
- JS: connectDragDrop(root, options) wires pointer and keyboard dragging; setDropState(target, state) sets data-drop; setDropEdge(item, edge) sets data-drop-edge; dragPreviewChip(label) creates a chip preview; dragHandleIcon (Hugeicons DragDropVertical SVG markup).
- A11y: Keyboard support: focused .ayy-drag-handle takes arrow keys (along the list to reorder, across to hop between areas); plain items take Alt + arrows. Screen readers: announce polite status updates on each move ("Item moved to position 2 of 4"). DragHandle button requires an aria-label naming the specific item ('Move Revenue', 'Move Priority'); its tooltip remains general ('Drag to reorder').

## Dialog (Overlays)
A window that opens over the page and asks for attention, for confirmations, forms and short tasks. It can be centred, slide in from the side as a drawer, or rise from the bottom on phones. It's built on the native dialog element, so focus and Esc work properly.
- Classes: `.ayy-dialog` `.ayy-dialog--sm` `.ayy-dialog--lg` `.ayy-dialog--xl` `.ayy-dialog--full` `.ayy-dialog--side-start` `.ayy-dialog--side-end` `.ayy-dialog--side-bottom` `.ayy-dialog__header` `.ayy-dialog__title` `.ayy-dialog__description` `.ayy-dialog__body` `.ayy-dialog__footer` `.ayy-dialog__close`
- States: hover, focus, open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` `full`
- Element: `<ayy-dialog open persistent>`, events `ayy-open-change`
- JS: dialogClass({ size?, side?, className? }); isBackdropClick(dialog, event); dialogCloseIcon (the Hugeicons close icon as SVG markup). Without any JS helper: dialog.showModal() / dialog.close(), or natively <button commandfor="id" command="show-modal"> in modern browsers.
- A11y: Always include a DialogTitle (or aria-label on the dialog). Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close (native behaviour). Esc closes; background is inert while open; page scroll is locked. A side modal is still a modal: same rules. A body with only text that scrolls needs tabindex="0" so keyboard users can scroll it; form fields inside make that unnecessary. Opening and closing fade/scale (side modals slide); the closing animation is skipped in browsers without @starting-style and under reduced motion.

## Popover (Overlays)
A small floating panel attached to a button, for extra content or controls that don't need a full dialog. It closes when you click outside or press Esc.
- Classes: `.ayy-popover` `.ayy-popover--sm` `.ayy-popover--lg`
- States: open
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- Element: `<ayy-popover side align open>`, events `ayy-open-change`
- JS: popoverClass constant; popoverSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class; md adds nothing); connectPopover(trigger, content, { side?, align?, offset?, crossAxisOffset?, boundary?, onToggle? }) → { open, close, isOpen, update, destroy }
- A11y: Give the content an accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at its heading). The trigger gets aria-expanded automatically; Esc and click-outside close it and focus returns to the trigger. It's not a focus trap — use Dialog when the user must finish something first.

## Tooltip (Overlays)
A short hint that appears when someone hovers or focuses an element, for naming icon buttons or giving a little extra detail. It stays inside the screen and never gets clipped.
- Classes: `.ayy-tooltip` `.ayy-tooltip__content`
- States: hover, focus, dismissed
- Element: `<ayy-tooltip side>`
- JS: tooltipClass, tooltipContentClass constants; generalActionLabel(label) extracts general verbs ("Edit", "Delete", "More actions") from specific aria-labels; enhanceTooltip(host) moves the bubble to the top layer and adds Esc (returns cleanup).
- A11y: Trigger must be focusable so keyboard users see it too. aria-describedby links trigger → tooltip (React does it automatically). Esc dismisses (WCAG 1.4.13); the bubble stays open while hovered.

## Alert (Feedback)
A message placed in the flow of a page to tell someone something they should notice, like a warning, an error or a confirmation. It can carry a title, a short explanation and actions.
- Classes: `.ayy-alert` `.ayy-alert--sm` `.ayy-alert--lg` `.ayy-alert--info` `.ayy-alert--success` `.ayy-alert--warning` `.ayy-alert--destructive` `.ayy-alert__title` `.ayy-alert__description` `.ayy-alert__actions`
- States: error
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: alertClass({ variant?, size?, className? }) → string; alertTitleClass, alertDescriptionClass, alertActionsClass constants
- A11y: Static alerts need no role. If it appears in response to an action, add role="alert" (urgent) or role="status" (polite). The icon is decorative: aria-hidden="true". The text must carry the meaning.

## Toast (Feedback)
A short message that appears briefly to confirm something happened. It shows above everything else on the page, including dialogs, and can carry images or previews as well as text.
- Classes: `.ayy-toaster` `.ayy-toaster__clear` `.ayy-toast` `.ayy-toast--success` `.ayy-toast--warning` `.ayy-toast--destructive` `.ayy-toast--info` `.ayy-toast--card` `.ayy-toast--card-split` `.ayy-toast--card-split--vertical` `.ayy-toast--long` `.ayy-toast--inline` `.ayy-toast--inline--success` `.ayy-toast--inline--busy` `.ayy-toast--inline--error` `.ayy-toast__icon` `.ayy-toast__content` `.ayy-toast__title` `.ayy-toast__description` `.ayy-toast__actions` `.ayy-toast__copy` `.ayy-toast__close` `.ayy-toast__backdrop` `.ayy-toast__image` `.ayy-toast__thumb` `.ayy-toast__media` `.ayy-toast__scrim` `.ayy-toast__center` `.ayy-toast__corner` `.ayy-toast__corner--top` `.ayy-toast__corner--top-start` `.ayy-toast__corner--bottom-start` `.ayy-toast__corner--bottom-end` `.ayy-toast__action` `.ayy-toast__status` `.ayy-toast__status--success` `.ayy-toast__status--busy` `.ayy-toast__status--error`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, error, leaving
