- A11y: The region is aria-live="polite"; destructive toasts use role="alert". Timers pause while the toaster stack or a toast is hovered or focused, so there's time to read it and reach its action. Messages are set with textContent — never HTML.

## Progress (Feedback)
A bar that shows how far along something is, or that work is happening when the end isn't known.
- Classes: `.ayy-progress` `.ayy-progress__bar` `.ayy-progress--sm` `.ayy-progress--lg` `.ayy-progress--success` `.ayy-progress--warning` `.ayy-progress--destructive` `.ayy-progress--ai` `.ayy-progress--indeterminate`
- States: error, loading
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: progressClass({ variant?, tone?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string (tone is a deprecated alias of variant)
- A11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them). Give it an accessible name: aria-label or aria-labelledby.

## Progress ring (Feedback)
Progress shown as a ring that fills up, for goals, timers and uploads in small spaces. It can show a known amount or an unknown one, with a value or an icon in the middle.
- Classes: `.ayy-progress-ring` `.ayy-progress-ring__svg` `.ayy-progress-ring__track` `.ayy-progress-ring__bar` `.ayy-progress-ring__label` `.ayy-progress-ring--sm` `.ayy-progress-ring--lg` `.ayy-progress-ring--xl` `.ayy-progress-ring--success` `.ayy-progress-ring--warning` `.ayy-progress-ring--destructive` `.ayy-progress-ring--ai` `.ayy-progress-ring--indeterminate`
- States: error, loading, empty
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg` `xl`
- JS: progressRingClass({ variant?, size?, indeterminate?, className? }) → string; progressRingSvg (the SVG markup to put first inside the ring); progressRingSizes. The fill colour can be overridden with --ayy-progress-color, as on Progress.
- A11y: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max (React sets them). Give it a name with aria-label or aria-labelledby. What the label in the middle says isn't read (a progressbar's content is presentational): put it in the name too ("Habit: 3 of 5 days this week"). The fill is drawn with the system highlight in High Contrast, the track in GrayText.

## Spinner (Feedback)
A small loading indicator for short waits, like inside a button or beside some text. For loading a larger area, use a skeleton instead.
- Classes: `.ayy-spinner` `.ayy-spinner--sm` `.ayy-spinner--lg`
- States: loading
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: spinnerClass({ size?, className? }) → string. Buttons: add aria-busy="true" and put an aria-hidden .ayy-spinner first inside (React: <Button loading>).
- A11y: A spinner on its own is a role="status" with an aria-label that says what's loading ("Loading invoices"). Inside a button, hide it (aria-hidden) and set aria-busy="true" on the button; the button's text still names it. Mark the region that's refreshing with aria-busy="true" until the new content is in. Under reduced motion it stops as a still ring; the label and aria-busy still say it's working.

## Skeleton (Feedback)
A placeholder shaped like the content that's loading, so the page doesn't jump when the real content arrives.
- Classes: `.ayy-skeleton` `.ayy-skeleton--text` `.ayy-skeleton--circle`
- States: loading
- JS: skeletonClass({ shape?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Skeletons are aria-hidden. Put aria-busy="true" on the container while loading, and remove it when content arrives. To name the loading region, give it role="status" and an aria-label — aria-label on a plain div is ignored. The shimmer stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Empty state (Feedback)
What a list, table or page shows when it has nothing to display yet, or nothing matches a search. It explains why it's empty and offers the action that fills it.
- Classes: `.ayy-empty-state` `.ayy-empty-state--bordered` `.ayy-empty-state--sm` `.ayy-empty-state--lg` `.ayy-empty-state--compact` `.ayy-empty-state__title` `.ayy-empty-state__description` `.ayy-empty-state__actions`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: emptyStateClass({ size?, bordered?, compact?, className? }) → string; emptyStateTitleClass, emptyStateDescriptionClass, emptyStateActionsClass constants.
- A11y: The title is a real heading at the level that fits the page (h2 under the page's h1, h3 inside a card). The icon tile is decorative: the title carries the meaning. When results change because of a search or filter, put the empty state inside a role="status" region (or announce the count) so screen reader users hear that nothing matched.

## Badge (Data display)
A small label that marks the status, category or count of something, like "New" or "Paid". It can include a status dot for things that are live.
- Classes: `.ayy-badge` `.ayy-badge--sm` `.ayy-badge--lg` `.ayy-badge--muted` `.ayy-badge--outline` `.ayy-badge--success` `.ayy-badge--warning` `.ayy-badge--destructive` `.ayy-badge--info` `.ayy-badge--ai` `.ayy-badge__dot` `.ayy-badge__dot--static`
- States: error
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: badgeClass({ variant?, size?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Colour is never the only signal — the label text must say the status. The dot is aria-hidden; it's decorative.

## Status dot (Data display)
A small coloured dot that shows the state of something, like someone being online, a live stream or a server's health.
- Classes: `.ayy-status-dot` `.ayy-status-dot--sm` `.ayy-status-dot--lg` `.ayy-status-dot--neutral` `.ayy-status-dot--success` `.ayy-status-dot--warning` `.ayy-status-dot--destructive` `.ayy-status-dot--info` `.ayy-status-dot--pulse`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: statusDotClass({ variant?, size?, pulse?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Colour is never the only signal — accompany standalone status dots with a text label or pass the label prop so screen readers announce it. When label is provided, sets role="status" and aria-label; when omitted, aria-hidden="true" treats the dot as decorative.

## Keyboard hint (Data display)
A small keycap for showing a keyboard key or shortcut in help text, menus and tooltips. Shortcuts adapt to the platform, so Mac users see their own symbols.
- Classes: `.ayy-kbd` `.ayy-kbd--sm` `.ayy-kbd--lg`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: kbdClass and keyboardHintClass constants; kbdSizeClass(size?) → string | undefined (the --sm / --lg class; md adds nothing). platformKeyLabel(key, platform) maps modifier names to platform symbols/names ("mod" → ⌘ on Mac, Ctrl on Windows/Linux; "meta" → ⌘ on Mac, Win on Windows, Super on Linux); platformKeyName(key, platform) gives its spoken name ("Command" for ⌘).
- A11y: Use the <kbd> element: screen readers and search know it's a key. Write modifier names out where symbols may not read well ("Ctrl" rather than "^"), or add aria-label="Command K" to a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> (screen readers pronounce "⌘" as "place of interest sign"). A shortcut hint doesn't replace aria-keyshortcuts on the control it triggers.

## Text highlight (Data display)
A way to mark text inside a sentence, for search matches or phrases that need attention. It's subtle by default, with colour variants for warnings, errors, successes and info.
- Classes: `.ayy-text-highlight` `.ayy-text-highlight--warning` `.ayy-text-highlight--destructive` `.ayy-text-highlight--success` `.ayy-text-highlight--info` `.ayy-text-highlight--orange`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: textHighlightClass({ variant?, className? }) → string; textHighlightParts(text, query) splits text into matching and non-matching segments.
- A11y: Uses the standard <mark> HTML tag for search and text highlights, recognised by assistive technology. Maintains readable contrast across light, dark, and high-contrast themes via color-mix() and light-dark(). Under Windows High Contrast mode (forced-colors), highlights switch to the system Highlight and HighlightText colours.

## Avatar (Data display)
A small picture that stands for a person or a workspace. When there's no image, or it fails to load, it shows initials instead.
- Classes: `.ayy-avatar` `.ayy-avatar--xs` `.ayy-avatar--sm` `.ayy-avatar--lg` `.ayy-avatar--xl` `.ayy-avatar--2xl` `.ayy-avatar--square` `.ayy-avatar__fallback` `.ayy-avatar__image` `.ayy-avatar-group`
- States: error
- Sizes: `xs` `sm` `md` `lg` `xl` `2xl`
- JS: avatarClass({ size?, shape?, className? }); avatarInitials(name); avatarGroupClass, avatarImageClass, avatarFallbackClass constants
- A11y: The name goes on the root (aria-label); the <img> has alt="" and the initials are aria-hidden, so it's announced once. Give an AvatarGroup an aria-label like "5 collaborators". A failed image is hidden by React or @danitesler/ayywi/elements so the initials show. With CSS alone it renders as a plain disc.

## Icon (Data display)
A single icon from the Hugeicons library that ayywi uses. It follows the colour and size of the text around it. Give it a name and an icon pack (Lucide, Tabler, Material Symbols, Feather) can draw it instead.
- Classes: `.ayy-icon` `.ayy-icon--sm` `.ayy-icon--md` `.ayy-icon--lg` `.ayy-icon--xl` `.ayy-icon--directional`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `auto` `sm` `md` `lg` `xl`
- JS: iconSvg(icon, { size?, directional?, name?, label?, strokeWidth?, className? }) → SVG markup for innerHTML, v-html, {@html} or server templates; iconClass({ size?, directional?, className? }); iconSizes; type IconData (Hugeicons' format). Icons come from `npm i @hugeicons/core-free-icons`: import { Search01Icon } from "@hugeicons/core-free-icons". Plain HTML: paste the SVG with class="ayy-icon". name writes data-ayy-icon, which a pack replaces: import "@danitesler/ayywi/icons/<pack>.css" and call setIconPack(pack) (or set data-ayy-icons on any element) to draw named icons in Lucide, Tabler, Material Symbols or Feather. strokeWidth only affects the inline Hugeicons paths; a pack keeps its own stroke.
- A11y: Icons are decorative by default (aria-hidden): the text next to them carries the meaning. When the icon is the only thing saying something (a status, a verified mark), give it a label: <Icon label="Deployed">, or role="img" + aria-label on the <svg>. Icon-only buttons: aria-label goes on the button, the icon stays decorative. Strokes use currentColor, so icons follow the theme and Windows High Contrast colours with no extra CSS.

## Icon tile (Data display)
A rounded app-icon tile that gives a product, plugin or service a recognisable mark, with the glyph tinted in its accent colour.
- Classes: `.ayy-icon-tile` `.ayy-icon-tile--sm` `.ayy-icon-tile--lg`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: iconTileClass({ size?, className? }) → string
- A11y: Usually decorative next to the product's name: aria-hidden="true" (React does this unless you pass aria-label). Standing alone, give it role="img" and an aria-label.

## Stat (Data display)
A big number with a short label, for headline figures like downloads, views or revenue.
- Classes: `.ayy-stat` `.ayy-stat--sm` `.ayy-stat__value` `.ayy-stat__unit` `.ayy-stat__label`
- States: none, it's static
- Sizes: `md` `sm`
- JS: statClass({ size?, className? }) → string; statValueClass, statUnitClass, statLabelClass constants.
- A11y: Write abbreviations the way they should be read, or add the full number: <span aria-hidden="true">200k</span><span class="ayy-sr-only">200,000</span>. Keep the unit as text, not only an icon.

## List (Data display)
Rows of people, records or settings, each with an image or icon, a title, a description and something at the end like a value or a control. A row can be a link.
- Classes: `.ayy-list` `.ayy-list--divided` `.ayy-list--compact` `.ayy-list__item` `.ayy-list__content` `.ayy-list__title` `.ayy-list__description` `.ayy-list__meta` `.ayy-list__link`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- JS: listClass({ divided?, compact?, className? }) → string; listItemClass, listContentClass, listTitleClass, listDescriptionClass, listMetaClass, listLinkClass constants.
- A11y: It's a real list: screen readers announce how many rows there are. One link per row, in the title, so a row is one tab stop with a meaningful name. Buttons and switches in the row are separate tab stops after it. Mark the open row with aria-current="page" (it's a page) or "true" (a selection in a list-detail view); it gets a tint and a heavier title, not just colour. A switch or checkbox in a settings row needs its label: make the title a <label for> pointing at it. Avatars and icons in the leading slot are decorative when the title names the row.

## Property list (Data display)
A record's attributes as a definition list: a muted term (an icon and a label) and its value, side by side, wrapping under each other when the value doesn't fit.
- Classes: `.ayy-property-list` `.ayy-property-list--sm` `.ayy-property-list--lg` `.ayy-property-list--compact` `.ayy-property-list__row` `.ayy-property-list__term` `.ayy-property-list__label` `.ayy-property-list__icon` `.ayy-property-list__value` `.ayy-property-list__empty`
- States: empty
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: propertyListClass({ size?, compact?, className? }) → string; propertyListRowClass, propertyListTermClass, propertyListLabelClass, propertyListIconClass, propertyListValueClass, propertyListEmptyClass constants.
- A11y: It's a real <dl>: screen readers announce a definition list and pair each term with its value. Each row is a <div> inside the <dl> (valid HTML) with exactly one <dt> and one <dd>, so the rows can wrap and flex. Icons in the term are decorative; the label names the row. An empty value says "Not set" in text, not a dash or a blank cell. A value edited in place keeps the nested InlineEdit's own label ("Change the version"); the term names the attribute, the control names the action.

## Swipe actions (Data display)
A list row that slides sideways to reveal actions, the way phone mail and task apps do. It works with touch, mouse and keyboard, and follows the reading direction.
- Classes: `.ayy-swipe` `.ayy-swipe__content` `.ayy-swipe__actions` `.ayy-swipe__actions--start` `.ayy-swipe__actions--end` `.ayy-swipe__action` `.ayy-swipe__action--primary` `.ayy-swipe__action--success` `.ayy-swipe__action--warning` `.ayy-swipe__action--info` `.ayy-swipe__action--destructive`
- States: focus, open, dragging
- Element: `<ayy-swipe>`, events `ayy-open-change`
- JS: connectSwipe(row, { onOpenChange? }) → { open(side), close(), destroy() } wires the gesture on plain markup: drag past half a tray to keep it open; a tap on the row, a tap elsewhere, Esc or an action closes it. swipeActionClass({ variant?, className? }); swipeActionVariants; swipeClass, swipeContentClass, swipeActionsClass constants.
- A11y: Swiping is a shortcut, never the only way: offer the same actions in the row's page or a Menu, since many people can't or don't swipe. The actions are real buttons after the content in the tab order; a tray with focus shows over the row, and Esc closes an open row. Labels stay visible under the icons, so the tint isn't the only cue. Undo destructive actions (a Toast with Undo) rather than asking for confirmation in the middle of a gesture.

## Timeline (Data display)
A list of events in time order, like a history, a changelog or a project's milestones, joined by a vertical line with status markers and timestamps.
- Classes: `.ayy-timeline` `.ayy-timeline--alternate` `.ayy-timeline__item` `.ayy-timeline__track` `.ayy-timeline__marker` `.ayy-timeline__marker--pulse` `.ayy-timeline__content` `.ayy-timeline__time` `.ayy-timeline__title` `.ayy-timeline__body`
- States: pulse
- JS: timelineClass({ alternate?, className? }) → string; timelineMarkerClass({ pulse?, className? }) → string; timelineItemClass, timelineTrackClass, timelineContentClass, timelineTimeClass, timelineTitleClass, timelineBodyClass constants.
- A11y: Rendered as an ordered list (<ol>) by default so screen readers announce the item count and sequence. Timestamps use the semantic <time> element with tabular numbers for consistent alignment and screen reader comprehension. Decorative markers and track lines are marked aria-hidden="true" to prevent screen reader noise; important status information should be in the title or body. Active pulse rings are visual enhancements; screen readers receive the active status via text in the title, body, or an accessible badge. Supports Windows High Contrast mode via @media (forced-colors: active) with system CanvasText, Canvas, and Highlight colors.

## Frame (Data display)
A browser window drawn around a screenshot, a video or a demo, for showing a product in context on marketing pages and in docs.
- Classes: `.ayy-frame` `.ayy-frame__bar` `.ayy-frame__title` `.ayy-frame__body`
- States: none, it's static
- JS: frameClass, frameBarClass, frameTitleClass, frameBodyClass constants.
- A11y: The screenshot is the content: give the <img> alt text that says what it shows, or wrap the frame in a <figure> with a <figcaption>. The dots are decoration (a pseudo-element).

## Chat (Data display)
The layout of a conversation, with other people's messages on one side and the reader's own on the other. It includes a typing indicator and quick-reply buttons, for assistants and support chats.
- Classes: `.ayy-chat` `.ayy-chat__message` `.ayy-chat__message--out` `.ayy-chat__bubble` `.ayy-chat__typing` `.ayy-chat__replies`
- States: loading
- JS: chatMessageClass({ direction?, className? }) → string; chatClass, chatBubbleClass, chatTypingClass, chatRepliesClass constants.
- A11y: Use role="log" on the conversation when messages arrive while the reader watches; they're announced politely, in order. The typing dots are an image with a name ("Dani is typing"); remove the element when the message lands. Quick replies are real buttons; after one is chosen, move focus to the next sensible place, not back to the top.

## Code block (Data display)
A container for showing code, with a header, a file name, a copy button and optional line numbers. It styles syntax highlighting without tying you to a particular highlighter.
- Classes: `.ayy-code-block` `.ayy-code-block--sm` `.ayy-code-block--lg` `.ayy-code-block--numbered` `.ayy-code-block__header` `.ayy-code-block__filename` `.ayy-code-block__actions` `.ayy-code-block__selector` `.ayy-code-block__chevron` `.ayy-code-block__menu` `.ayy-code-block__copy` `.ayy-code-block__pre` `.ayy-code-block__code` `.ayy-code-block__line` `.ayy-token-keyword` `.ayy-token-string` `.ayy-token-comment` `.ayy-token-function` `.ayy-token-number` `.ayy-token-operator` `.ayy-token-tag` `.ayy-token-attribute` `.ayy-token-property` `.ayy-token-punctuation` `.ayy-token-boolean`
- States: hover, pressed, focus, copied
- Sizes: `sm` `md` `lg`
- JS: codeBlockClass({ size?, numbered?, className? }) → string; codeBlockHeaderClass({ className? }); codeBlockFilenameClass({ className? }); codeBlockActionsClass({ className? }); codeBlockSelectorClass({ className? }); codeBlockChevronClass({ className? }); codeBlockMenuClass({ className? }); codeBlockCopyClass({ className? }); codeBlockPreClass({ className? }); codeBlockCodeClass({ className? }); highlightCode(code, language?) → string; tokenizeCode(code, language?) → CodeToken[]; copyCodeBlock(button, { code?, timeout?, label?, copiedLabel? }) copies the code and shows the copied state; syncCodeBlockSelector(selectOrLang, codeBlock?) switches a code block to the chosen language: its label, and the code (and file name) from the block's own <template data-language="…" data-filename="…"> for that language, else the code stays; SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES, LANGUAGE_SNIPPETS; codeBlockCopyIcon, codeBlockCheckIcon (SVG markup).
- A11y: Pre element is scrollable via keyboard by adding tabindex="0". Copy button has an accessible label (aria-label) and announces state changes. Line numbers use CSS counters with user-select: none to avoid being copied into the clipboard. Syntax token classes maintain WCAG AA 4.5:1 contrast against the surface background in light and dark themes.

## Table (Data display)
Data table with quiet hairlines, muted sentence-case headers and hover rows, styled on plain table elements under .ayy-table. Optional frame with toolbar and pager; densities, column lines, sticky header, pinned and resizable columns; sortable, selectable (including drag-to-select across rows), expandable, grouped, linked and disabled rows; column menus with icons, insertion and wrapping; inline editable, empty, truncated and media cells; row actions. Cell content stays inside its column and ends in … unless the column wraps.
- Classes: `.ayy-table-container` `.ayy-table__toolbar` `.ayy-table__heading` `.ayy-table__title` `.ayy-table__description` `.ayy-table__tools` `.ayy-table__pager` `.ayy-table-wrap` `.ayy-table` `.ayy-table--compact` `.ayy-table--spacious` `.ayy-table--bordered` `.ayy-table--sticky` `.ayy-table--fixed` `.ayy-table--reorderable` `.ayy-table__draggable` `.ayy-table__column-header` `.ayy-table__column-label` `.ayy-table__column-icon` `.ayy-table__add-column` `.ayy-table__wrap` `.ayy-table__num` `.ayy-table__sort` `.ayy-table__resize` `.ayy-table__select` `.ayy-table__reorder` `.ayy-table__pin` `.ayy-table__pin--end` `.ayy-table__truncate` `.ayy-table__edit` `.ayy-table__media` `.ayy-table__secondary` `.ayy-table__expand` `.ayy-table__detail` `.ayy-table__group` `.ayy-table__empty` `.ayy-table__row-link` `.ayy-table__actions` `.ayy-table__row-actions` `.ayy-table__row-actions--reveal`
- States: hover, focus, disabled, selected, error, loading, sorted, expanded, resizing, reordering, row-reordering
- Element: `<ayy-table>`, events `ayy-sort`, `ayy-selection-change`, `ayy-expand-change`, `ayy-column-resize`, `ayy-cell-edit`, `ayy-column-reorder`, `ayy-row-reorder`, `ayy-column-action`
- JS: tableClass({ compact?, spacious?, bordered?, sticky?, fixed?, reorderable?, className? }); tableRowActionsClass({ reveal?, className? }); tablePinClassName(pin); a table…Class constant per class; nextSortDirection(current); compareValues(a, b, direction?) sorts numbers ("$1,240", "12 GB") by value, text naturally, empty last; connectTableResize(table, { onResize? }); connectTableDragSelect(table, { onRowChange? }); connectTableEdit(table, { onCellEdit? }); connectTableColumnReorder(table, { onColumnReorder?, selector? }); connectTableColumns(table, { onColumnAction? }); connectTable(table, { onColumnAction?, onSort?, onSelectionChange?, onExpandChange?, onResize?, onCellEdit?, onColumnReorder? }) wires plain markup (used by <ayy-table>).
- A11y: Use real <th> cells with scope (React sets scope="col"); a cell naming its row can be <th scope="row">. Name the table: a <caption>, or aria-labelledby pointing at the .ayy-table__title. Sort buttons are reachable by Tab and announced with aria-sort; only the sorted column carries it. Row checkboxes, expand buttons and row action buttons need aria-labels naming their row ("Select INV-1042", "Show details for INV-1042"); point an expand button's aria-controls at its detail row. Resize handles are focusable separators with aria-valuenow in px: arrow keys resize (Shift: bigger steps), Home/End jump to the limits. Set aria-busy="true" while rows load, and aria-disabled="true" on rows that can't be acted on (disable their controls too).

## Grid (Data display)
A grid of cards that can be selected, for media, projects, posts and records. It combines card selection, quick actions on each item and a select-all control, and works with the Action bar.
- Classes: `.ayy-grid-wrap` `.ayy-grid__toolbar` `.ayy-grid__select-all` `.ayy-grid` `.ayy-grid--compact` `.ayy-grid__item` `.ayy-grid__media` `.ayy-grid__header` `.ayy-grid__select` `.ayy-grid__actions` `.ayy-grid__actions--reveal` `.ayy-grid__title` `.ayy-grid__description` `.ayy-grid__body` `.ayy-grid__footer`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- Element: `<ayy-grid>`, events `ayy-selection-change`
- JS: gridClass({ compact?, className? }) → string; gridItemActionsClass({ reveal?, className? }) → string; gridWrapClass, gridToolbarClass, gridSelectAllClass, gridItemClass, gridMediaClass, gridHeaderClass, gridSelectClass, gridActionsClass, gridTitleClass, gridDescriptionClass, gridBodyClass, gridFooterClass constants; connectGrid(root, { onSelectionChange? }) wires select-all, card checkboxes, card-body click selection and Shift+click range selection (used by <ayy-grid>).
- A11y: Each selectable card contains a native Checkbox in GridItemSelect with an aria-label naming the item ("Select Hero screenshot"). Selected cards carry aria-selected="true" and a 2px border (Highlight outline in High Contrast mode), never colour alone. Per-card icon buttons and ⋯ DropdownMenu triggers carry an aria-label naming the item ("More actions for Hero screenshot"). GridItemActions with reveal uses opacity so controls remain in the Tab order and become visible on :focus-within.

## Chart (Data display)
Charts for reading data at a glance: bars, lines, areas, pies and donuts, scatters, gauges and more. They're drawn with plain markup and CSS instead of a charting library, and each comes with a data table for screen readers. Colours, hover details and a switchable legend are built in.
- Classes: `.ayy-chart` `.ayy-chart--stacked` `.ayy-chart--values` `.ayy-chart--horizontal` `.ayy-chart--histogram` `.ayy-chart--combo` `.ayy-chart--waterfall` `.ayy-chart--pie` `.ayy-chart--gauge` `.ayy-chart--radar` `.ayy-chart__plot` `.ayy-chart__tick` `.ayy-chart__bars` `.ayy-chart__column` `.ayy-chart__bar` `.ayy-chart__bar--up` `.ayy-chart__bar--down` `.ayy-chart__svg` `.ayy-chart__series` `.ayy-chart__series--compare` `.ayy-chart__line` `.ayy-chart__area` `.ayy-chart__gradient` `.ayy-chart__labels` `.ayy-chart__axis` `.ayy-chart__dot` `.ayy-chart__ring` `.ayy-chart__track` `.ayy-chart__slice` `.ayy-chart__total` `.ayy-chart__total-value` `.ayy-chart__grid` `.ayy-chart__label` `.ayy-chart__tooltip` `.ayy-chart__tooltip--static` `.ayy-chart__tooltip-title` `.ayy-chart__tooltip-row` `.ayy-chart__tooltip-name` `.ayy-chart__tooltip-value` `.ayy-chart__hits` `.ayy-chart__hit` `.ayy-chart__marker` `.ayy-chart__legend` `.ayy-chart__legend-toggle` `.ayy-chart__legend-item` `.ayy-chart__legend-item--compare` `.ayy-chart__legend-item--line` `.ayy-chart__swatch` `.ayy-chart__legend-value` `.ayy-bar-list` `.ayy-bar-list__item` `.ayy-bar-list__label` `.ayy-bar-list__value` `.ayy-sparkline` `.ayy-heatmap` `.ayy-heatmap__row` `.ayy-heatmap__label` `.ayy-heatmap__cell` `.ayy-heatmap__key` `.ayy-funnel` `.ayy-funnel__step` `.ayy-funnel__label` `.ayy-funnel__bar` `.ayy-funnel__value` `.ayy-funnel__rate`
- States: hover, focus, selected
- JS: chartScale(values, { ticks?, min?, max? }) → { min, max, ticks } with a round top; chartPercent(value, max, min?) → 0–100 for --ayy-value; chartPath(values, { min?, max?, smooth?, step?, band?, base? }) → { line, area } path data for the 0 0 100 100 box (step: steps; band: points over column centres; base: the area's floor, for stacking); chartStack(series, { percent? }) → each series' running top; chartBins(values, { bins?, min?, max? }) → { edges, counts } for a histogram; chartSlices(values, { total? }) → [{ start, value }] shares for ring slices; chartRadar(values, { min?, max? }) → a closed path and chartRadarPoint(index, count, share?, radius?) → { x, y } for spokes and labels; chartWaterfall(steps) → [{ from, to, change }]; chartColors(target?, count?) → resolved rgb() strings and chartTheme(target?) → { colors, text, muted, grid, surface, fontFamily } for canvas libraries (Chart.js, ECharts); chartClass({ stacked?, values?, horizontal?, type?, className? }) with type one of chartTypes (histogram, combo, waterfall, pie, gauge, radar), chartSeriesClass({ compare?, className? }), chartLegendItemClass({ compare?, line?, className? }) and part class constants. toggleChartLegend(button) is what @danitesler/ayywi/elements runs when an .ayy-chart__legend-toggle is clicked in plain HTML: it flips aria-pressed and sets data-hidden on the same-numbered bars or series (donuts, pies and stacked areas need React to work their shares out again).
- A11y: The drawing is aria-hidden. The numbers go in a table with a <caption> saying what the chart shows, inside a <div class="ayy-sr-only"> (as React renders it): a table can't be narrower than its content, so hiding the table itself lets a long caption widen the page. Add a visible Table if people need to compare values. Don't rely on colour alone: a legend names the series in the same order, the comparison series is dashed, and a title or a Stat states the takeaway ("Up 12% on last week"). Series tokens keep 3:1 against every surface in every theme. In High Contrast bars and lines take system colours, alternating between CanvasText and Highlight. A Sparkline with a label is an image with that name; give it the trend in words ("Revenue, last 14 days, up 12%"). A gauge is one value, so it's a meter: role="meter" with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, aria-valuenow, an aria-valuetext in words ("$7.2K of $10K") and a name. A funnel and a bar list are text already and need no table. Waterfall changes are signed (+$6.4K, −$1.3K) as well as coloured, and a donut's legend gives each share as a number.
